questions.stem: A 63-year-old man has had double vision and a dull ache above his left eye since he woke up 2 days ago. He has type 2 diabetes and hypertension and often skips his medications. The left upper eyelid droops. When he looks straight ahead, the left eye points down and out. Both pupils are 3 mm and react briskly to light. The rest of the neurologic exam is normal. Laboratory studies show: fasting glucose 248 mg/dL, hemoglobin A1c 10.2%, sodium 138 mEq/L, creatinine 1.1 mg/dL. Which mechanism most likely explains his findings?
choices: Ischemia of the inner part of the oculomotor nerve, sparing its outer fibers
Compression of the oculomotor nerve by a posterior communicating artery aneurysm
Herniation of the medial temporal lobe through the tentorial notch
Antibodies against acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction
Septic thrombosis of the cavernous sinus spreading from the face
questions.explanation: Ptosis and a **down-and-out** eye with a **normal pupil** in a patient with poorly controlled diabetes is a **microvascular (ischemic) CN III palsy**. Ischemia damages the core of the nerve, while the pupillary fibers on its **surface** keep their blood supply. A **posterior communicating artery aneurysm** is the tempting choice, but compression reaches those superficial fibers early and typically gives a **dilated, poorly reactive pupil**. Uncal herniation also compresses CN III from outside and occurs with a falling level of consciousness.
questions.explanation_pt: Ptose e olho **para baixo e para fora** com **pupila normal** em paciente com diabetes mal controlado indicam **paralisia microvascular (isquêmica) do NC III**. A isquemia lesa o centro do nervo, enquanto as fibras pupilares da **superfície** mantêm sua irrigação. O **aneurisma da artéria comunicante posterior** é a alternativa tentadora, mas a compressão atinge cedo essas fibras superficiais e costuma causar **pupila dilatada e pouco reativa**. A herniação uncal também comprime o NC III por fora e ocorre com rebaixamento do nível de consciência.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman has had blurred vision in her right eye for 4 days. Moving the eye hurts. Visual acuity is 20/200 in the right eye and 20/20 in the left eye. Colors look faded when she uses the right eye. In a dim room, light shone into the left eye makes both pupils constrict. When the light is moved quickly to the right eye, both pupils dilate. Eye movements are full, and there is no ptosis. Where is the lesion that best explains her findings?
choices: Right oculomotor nerve
Right Edinger-Westphal nucleus
Optic chiasm
Right optic nerve
Left optic tract
questions.explanation: Both pupils dilate when the light moves to the right eye, so less light signal enters the brainstem from that eye: a **relative afferent pupillary defect** from a **right optic nerve** lesion (here, likely **optic neuritis**). Because both pupils still move together, the efferent pathways are intact. A **right CN III** lesion is the tempting choice, but an efferent defect leaves the right pupil large and sluggish whichever eye is lit, and usually comes with ptosis or weak eye movements. A left optic tract lesion would cause a right homonymous hemianopia, not a loss of acuity in one eye.
questions.explanation_pt: As duas pupilas dilatam quando a luz passa para o olho direito, ou seja, chega menos sinal luminoso ao tronco encefálico por esse olho: um **defeito pupilar aferente relativo** por lesão do **nervo óptico direito** (aqui, provavelmente **neurite óptica**). Como as pupilas continuam se movendo juntas, as vias eferentes estão íntegras. A lesão do **NC III direito** é a alternativa tentadora, mas um defeito eferente deixa a pupila direita grande e lenta seja qual for o olho iluminado, e costuma vir com ptose ou limitação da motilidade ocular. Uma lesão do trato óptico esquerdo causaria hemianopsia homônima direita, e não perda de acuidade em um olho.

questions.stem: A 61-year-old man comes to the clinic because, for the past month, everything sometimes looks slightly blue for a few hours. This happens only on evenings when he takes a drug that he recently started for erectile dysfunction. Visual acuity, visual fields, pupils and fundoscopy are normal. By which mechanism does the drug most likely cause this symptom?
choices: Blockade of muscarinic receptors in the ciliary muscle
Activation of transducin in the absence of light
Depletion of 11-cis-retinal in the retinal pigment epithelium
Contraction of the iris sphincter, narrowing the pupil
Inhibition of the photoreceptor enzyme that degrades cGMP
questions.explanation: **Sildenafil** blocks PDE-5 in the penis, but it also partly inhibits **PDE-6**, the photoreceptor enzyme that breaks down **cGMP** during phototransduction. Changing cGMP signaling in the cones alters color perception and gives a temporary **blue tint**. **Transducin activation** is tempting because it is a step of the same cascade, but the drug acts on the enzyme downstream of transducin, not on transducin itself. A lack of 11-cis-retinal (vitamin A deficiency) causes night blindness, not a blue tint.
questions.explanation_pt: A **sildenafila** bloqueia a PDE-5 no pênis, mas também inibe parcialmente a **PDE-6**, a enzima dos fotorreceptores que degrada o **GMPc** durante a fototransdução. A alteração da sinalização do GMPc nos cones muda a percepção das cores e causa uma **visão azulada** transitória. A **ativação da transducina** é tentadora porque faz parte da mesma cascata, mas o fármaco age na enzima a jusante da transducina, e não na própria transducina. A falta de 11-cis-retinal (deficiência de vitamina A) causa cegueira noturna, e não visão azulada.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old woman has had brief spells of severe spinning for 2 weeks. Each spell starts when she lies down or rolls over in bed and stops within 30 seconds. Between spells she feels well. Hearing is normal, and she has no tinnitus. Her head is turned 45 degrees to the right and she is quickly lowered backward. After a delay of a few seconds, a torsional, upbeating nystagmus appears and fades within 20 seconds. Repeating the maneuver produces a weaker response. Which mechanism best explains her vertigo?
choices: Excess endolymph that distends the membranous labyrinth
Loose calcium carbonate crystals moving inside a semicircular canal
Viral inflammation of the vestibular part of the eighth cranial nerve
Ischemia of the cerebellum in the posterior inferior cerebellar artery territory
A Schwann cell tumor at the cerebellopontine angle
questions.explanation: Spells of seconds triggered by head position, with a delayed, short-lasting and **fatigable** nystagmus on the Dix-Hallpike test, are **benign paroxysmal positional vertigo**. Loose **otoconia** move inside the **posterior semicircular canal** and stimulate it whenever the head moves in that plane. **Vestibular neuritis** is the tempting choice, but it causes **constant** vertigo for days, not short positional spells. Ménière disease causes attacks lasting hours with tinnitus and hearing loss, and a cerebellar stroke gives nystagmus that does not fatigue, often with other neurologic signs.
questions.explanation_pt: Crises de segundos desencadeadas pela posição da cabeça, com nistagmo com latência, breve e **fatigável** na manobra de Dix-Hallpike, indicam **vertigem posicional paroxística benigna**. **Otocônias** soltas se movem dentro do **canal semicircular posterior** e o estimulam sempre que a cabeça se move nesse plano. A **neurite vestibular** é a alternativa tentadora, mas causa vertigem **contínua** por dias, e não crises posicionais curtas. A doença de Ménière causa crises de horas com zumbido e perda auditiva, e o AVC cerebelar causa nistagmo que não se fatiga, muitas vezes com outros sinais neurológicos.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man says he can hear people talk but often cannot understand them, especially in noisy restaurants. He has the most trouble with his granddaughter's high voice. The ear canals and tympanic membranes are normal. The Weber test does not lateralize, and air conduction is better than bone conduction in both ears. Pure-tone audiometry gives the same results in both ears (normal is 25 dB or less). Air-conduction thresholds: 250 Hz, 15 dB; 1000 Hz, 20 dB; 2000 Hz, 35 dB; 4000 Hz, 55 dB; 8000 Hz, 70 dB. Bone-conduction thresholds match the air thresholds at every frequency tested. Where is the damage most likely located?
choices: Hair cells near the apex of the cochlea
Stapes footplate at the oval window
Hair cells near the base of the cochlea
Vestibulocochlear nerve at the cerebellopontine angle
Tympanic membrane
questions.explanation: Equal air and bone thresholds with a normal Weber and Rinne mean **symmetric sensorineural** loss, and the loss grows with frequency: this is **presbycusis**. The **base** of the cochlea has a narrow, stiff basilar membrane that responds to **high** frequencies, and its hair cells are lost first with age and noise. The **apex** is the tempting distractor, but it is wide and flexible and codes **low** tones, which are normal here. A vestibular schwannoma is usually one-sided, and stapes or tympanic membrane problems cause conductive loss with a gap between bone and air thresholds.
questions.explanation_pt: Limiares aéreos e ósseos iguais, com Weber e Rinne normais, indicam perda **neurossensorial simétrica**, e a perda aumenta com a frequência: é **presbiacusia**. A **base** da cóclea tem membrana basilar estreita e rígida, que responde a frequências **agudas**, e suas células ciliadas são perdidas primeiro com a idade e o ruído. O **ápice** é o distrator tentador, mas é largo e flexível e codifica sons **graves**, que aqui estão normais. O schwannoma vestibular costuma ser unilateral, e problemas do estribo ou da membrana timpânica causam perda condutiva, com diferença entre os limiares ósseo e aéreo.

questions.stem: A 74-year-old man suddenly lost vision in his right eye 1 hour ago. He has no eye pain, headache or jaw pain. He has hypertension and stopped taking his anticoagulant last month. Vital signs: pulse 108/min and irregularly irregular, blood pressure 156/92 mm Hg, temperature 36.8°C. With the right eye he can see only hand movements; the left eye is normal. The right eye has a relative afferent pupillary defect. Fundoscopy of the right eye shows a pale, swollen retina, thin arterioles, and a bright red spot at the center of the macula. Which vessel is most likely blocked?
choices: Central retinal vein
Central retinal artery
Short posterior ciliary arteries
Left posterior cerebral artery
Right middle cerebral artery
questions.explanation: Sudden painless loss of vision in one eye with a pale retina and a **cherry-red spot** is **central retinal artery occlusion**, here most likely from an **embolus** formed in the left atrium during **atrial fibrillation**. The inner retina becomes ischemic and opaque, but the thin fovea lets the normal **choroidal** circulation show through. **Central retinal vein occlusion** is the tempting choice, but it shows widespread **hemorrhages** and dilated, tortuous veins. A posterior cerebral artery stroke causes a homonymous field defect in both eyes with a normal fundus.
questions.explanation_pt: Perda visual súbita e indolor em um olho, com retina pálida e **mancha vermelho-cereja**, indica **oclusão da artéria central da retina**, aqui provavelmente por **êmbolo** formado no átrio esquerdo na **fibrilação atrial**. A retina interna fica isquêmica e opaca, mas a fóvea, mais fina, deixa aparecer a circulação normal da **coroide**. A **oclusão da veia central da retina** é a alternativa tentadora, mas mostra **hemorragias** difusas e veias dilatadas e tortuosas. Um AVC da artéria cerebral posterior causa defeito de campo homônimo nos dois olhos, com fundo de olho normal.

questions.stem: A 66-year-old woman with primary open-angle glaucoma starts a once-daily eye drop in her left eye only. Six months later, the intraocular pressure in that eye is lower. She notices that her left iris has become browner than the right one and that her left eyelashes are longer and thicker. By which mechanism does this drug lower intraocular pressure?
choices: Blockade of beta receptors in the ciliary epithelium, reducing aqueous production
Inhibition of carbonic anhydrase in the ciliary epithelium
Contraction of the ciliary muscle, which opens the trabecular meshwork
Increased drainage of aqueous humor through the uveoscleral pathway
Stimulation of alpha-2 receptors, reducing aqueous production
questions.explanation: Darkening of the iris and growth of the eyelashes in the treated eye are typical of a **prostaglandin F2-alpha analog** such as **latanoprost**. It lowers pressure mainly by increasing **uveoscleral outflow** of aqueous humor. **Timolol** is the tempting choice because it is also a common first drop, but it lowers aqueous production and does not change iris color; its risks are bradycardia and bronchospasm. Pilocarpine opens the trabecular meshwork by contracting the ciliary muscle and also causes miosis.
questions.explanation_pt: Escurecimento da íris e crescimento dos cílios no olho tratado são típicos de um **análogo da prostaglandina F2-alfa**, como a **latanoprosta**. Ele reduz a pressão principalmente ao aumentar o **escoamento uveoescleral** do humor aquoso. O **timolol** é a alternativa tentadora por também ser um colírio inicial comum, mas reduz a produção de aquoso e não muda a cor da íris; seus riscos são bradicardia e broncoespasmo. A pilocarpina abre a malha trabecular ao contrair o músculo ciliar e também causa miose.

questions.stem: A 46-year-old woman says that over the past year she has had to hold her phone and books farther away to read them. In dim light, reading is even harder. Her distance vision is still clear. Pupils react normally to light and to a near target, and the eyes converge normally. The lenses are clear, and fundoscopy is normal. Which change best explains her symptom?
choices: Stiffening of the lens with age, so it cannot become rounder
Loss of parasympathetic input from CN III to the ciliary muscle
Elongation of the eyeball that focuses images in front of the retina
Uneven curvature of the cornea in different directions
Opacification of the lens nucleus that scatters light
questions.explanation: This is **presbyopia**: for near vision, the **ciliary muscle** contracts, the **zonules relax**, and the lens rounds up by its own elasticity. With age the lens becomes **stiffer**, so it cannot round up enough even when the zonules relax. **Loss of parasympathetic input** is the tempting choice, but it would also leave the pupil large and unable to constrict to a near target, and her pupils are normal. A long eyeball (myopia) blurs distance vision, and a cataract would show an opaque lens.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **presbiopia**: para a visão de perto, o **músculo ciliar** contrai, as **fibras zonulares relaxam** e o cristalino se arredonda pela própria elasticidade. Com a idade o cristalino fica **mais rígido** e não consegue se arredondar o suficiente, mesmo com as fibras zonulares relaxadas. A **perda do estímulo parassimpático** é a alternativa tentadora, mas também deixaria a pupila grande e sem constrição para um alvo próximo, e as pupilas dela são normais. Um globo ocular longo (miopia) borra a visão de longe, e a catarata mostraria um cristalino opaco.
